back: A person who supports a particular idea or party (e.g. an adherent of a political movement).
Someone who has taken on a new set of beliefs (e.g. a convert to Buddhism).
Someone who believes there should be extreme political change, either of a left- or right-wing nature.
(disapproving) Someone who is opposed to change or new ideas.
(disapproving) Someone with strong unreasonable beliefs who thinks anyone with other beliefs is wrong.
The unquestioning acceptance that something is true as a basis for a theory.
To abolish or get rid of something completely (e.g. to eradicate exploitation or poverty).
To suggest a basic principle (verb) or the principle itself (noun) as a basis for reasoning.
Describing someone who is too willing to believe what they are told; easily deceived.
Not wanting or being able to believe something; showing disbelief.
(formal) The acceptance of something as true (e.g. to give credence to a hypothesis).
Trusting and sincere, often in a way that seems foolish or unsuspecting.
An explanation or argument that is seemingly likely to be true (opposite: implausible).
One of the basic principles or beliefs on which a theory or philosophy is based.

front: give someone the benefit of the doubt
back: To accept that someone is telling the truth even though you are not certain.
